answer: Identity cost-ladder via usage history. Each new identity starts at a low trust tier, and moving up requires sustained transaction volume where every counterparty sees a mirror of prior behavior before committing value. An attacker must fund real, non-reversible work across many identities, and the marginal cost per identity rises because fresh identities earn less; this creates a ripple of wasted spend for anyone scaling up fakes. Duplicates therefore drown in their own setup expense, filtered naturally like silt settling in a river rather than blocked by a gate.
